claims.prior_art: Published as a(3) of OEIS A398541. Nothing new is asserted here.
claims.notes: The smallest end-to-end case, kept because it exercises every gate rule against real artifacts rather than fixtures: an avoiding coloring of {1..8} on the lower side, and UNSAT at N=9 from all three encoders on the upper side. Solved with kissat 4.0.1; the gate regenerates each instance from (N,k,l,encoder) and matches the recorded sha256 without a solver present.

claims.prior_art: The bound N(17,2) >= 273 is published by T. A. Lystad, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21840279 (v1.3 bundle), with a periodic witness at N = 272. This repository claims no priority for it.
claims.notes: a(17) of A398541 is open; this is the lower side of it. The witness was re-derived from the published description rather than copied - nine +1 then eight -1, period 17, tiled 16 times - and re-checked with nk2/evaluator.py, which reports a maximum |AP sum| of 1 over all 2176 seventeen-term APs in {1..272}. Every such AP has 1 <= d <= 16, so it meets each residue class mod 17 exactly once. No upper bound is claimed: N(17,2) <= V would need UNSAT at N = V from two encoders and no such run exists.
